title: Kinect v1 as a measuring instrument (depth lattice, noise populations, capabilities)
description:
In plain words. The Kinect is a depth camera made for the Xbox 360: point it at a room and every pixel comes back with a distance in millimetres. We measured one unit the way a lab measures an instrument. It cannot report just any distance: between 1 and 4 metres it has exactly 259 possible values, all of them listed by a table that PrimeSense, the sensor's designer, published, with nothing fitted. Microsoft's software and the open-source drivers use the same table but sit half a step apart. About 1 % of the pixels carry 95 % of the noise, and the sensor drifts by +8.2 mm in its first 6 minutes of warming up at 2.5 m. The count itself was first reported in 2014; what is added here is the exact formula match, the driver offset, the noise split and a map of what this hardware can and cannot do.

The idea in one picture. a ladder leaning into the room. The sensor can only stand on a rung, never between two. At 1 m the rungs are about 3 mm apart; at 3 m they are about 26 mm apart, so far objects get coarser readings. Where the picture breaks. a real ladder has evenly spaced rungs, while these are evenly spaced in one over the distance; and a pixel does not stand still on its rung, because noise can make it hop to the next one.

For specialists. Measurements and tools for one Xbox 360 Kinect (PrimeSense PS1080) via Kinect for Windows SDK 1.8. The SDK's depth output is exactly PrimeSense's published shift-to-depth table at phase 0 (259 values between 1 and 4 m, 345 in the 0.8-4 m window, matching a 2014 census), whereas libfreenect and OpenNI sit at phase 0.5, so the drivers' value sets interleave by half a step. The SDK's calibration blob, read through documented calls only, contains the PrimeSense registration block; the SDK uses it only for depth-to-colour registration, while its 3-D coordinates use a nominal pinhole. Also: three range-dependent per-pixel noise populations, a short-range temporal correlation (detrended), warm-up drift, capability confirmations (Bayer mosaic, 10-bit IR, hardware gates, extended depth, 4-channel audio, accelerometer) and a lateral-scale check against a factory-sized reference (+0.45 % to +1.74 %; no verdict by its sealed rule). Every claim has its script and status; corrections are listed first.

Links. Repository, with a plain-language guide: github.com/Hashirama1337s/kinect-v1-depth-levels. All projects: the Moki & Julio lab map.

Prepared with AI assistance; what was checked, and by what, is stated above.
